title: Bounded modification genus for inseparable prime-degree covers
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian complete regular local ring of dimension $2$ and characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, its field of fractions. Let $L/K$ be an inseparable field extension of degree $p$ [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$, namely the subring of elements of $L$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then reduction to rational singularities is possible for $S$ [def-per-rational-surface-singularity].

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-inseparable-surface-differential-data] to $A=R$ and $L/K$. Fix its $k,x,y,g,f,A_0,r$, so $L=K(g)$, $g^p=f\in R$, $f\notin K^p$, $R$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $A_0$, and $\Omega_{R/A_0}$ is free of rank $r$ with $\mathrm df\ne0$. In particular the degree-$p$ extension is purely inseparable. All these are choices independent of any modification.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; first paragraph: choosing the coefficient subfield and differential coordinates.

proof.text: The complete Noetherian local ring $R$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Apply [lem-per-normal-surface-cover-completed-degree] to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $L/K$: its normalization $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is finite, normal, integral, excellent and Noetherian of dimension $2$. The regular ring $R$ is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-integral-prime-unique] there is exactly one prime of $S$ over the maximal ideal of $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], every maximal ideal of $S$ contracts to the unique maximal ideal of $R$. Thus $S$ is local. Finally excellence implies Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata]. Thus the bounded-genus definition applies to $S$.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; normalization and local Nagata hypotheses implicit in the statement and final application of 0B4S.

proof.text: Put $W=\bigwedge_R^r\Omega_{R/A_0}$, a free rank-one $R$-module. By [lem-per-coherent-normal-surface-trace-calculus], $W[2]$ is normalized dualizing and $\omega_S=\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,W)$ is a finite canonical module with $\omega_S[2]$ normalized dualizing. Apply [lem-per-inseparable-differential-trace] in degree $r$ to $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$. Its coherence hypothesis holds since $\Omega_{R/A_0}$ is finite free. Since $W$ is already its double dual, this gives $T:\Omega^r_{S/A_0}\to W$. The source is coherent: $S$ is a finite-type $R$-algebra, so $\Omega_{S/A_0}$ is generated by the finite basis of $\Omega_{R/A_0}$ and the differentials of finitely many algebra generators; on the Noetherian ring $S$ the kernel of each map from a finite free module is finite. Its exterior powers are coherent as finite quotients of finite tensor powers. Finite adjunction defines the $S$-linear map $c:\Omega^r_{S/A_0}\to\omega_S$ by $c(\alpha)(s)=T(s\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; canonical differential trace and its finite-duality adjoint c.

proof.text: Choose basis vectors $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_{r-1}$ complementary to a nonzero coefficient of $\mathrm df$ in a basis of $\Omega_{R/A_0}$. Then $\theta=\eta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\eta_{r-1}\wedge\mathrm df$ is nonzero in $W$. For $0\leq i<p$ put $\alpha_i=\eta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\eta_{r-1}\wedge g^{p-1-i}\mathrm dg$ and $\varphi_i=c(\alpha_i)$. The formula in [lem-per-inseparable-differential-trace] gives $\varphi_i(g^j)=\delta_{ij}\theta$. Indeed, for $j<i$ the exponent $p-1-i+j$ is below $p-1$; for $j=i$ it is $p-1$; for $j>i$, reduce $g^{p-1-i+j}$ to $f g^{j-i-1}$, whose exponent is below $p-1$. Thus these $p$ functionals form a $K$-basis of $\operatorname{Hom}_K(L,W\otimes_RK)$, using the basis $1,g,\ldots,g^{p-1}$ from Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; claim: the explicitly constructed forms and the Kronecker-delta trace calculation.

proof.text: Set $Q=\omega_S/\operatorname{im}c$. The finite $R$-module $\omega_S$ makes $Q$ finite. Step 4 shows that every element of $Q$ becomes zero after inverting $R\setminus\{0\}$. Choose generators $q_1,\ldots,q_n$ and, for each generator, a nonzero $a_j\in R$ with $a_jq_j=0$, as the definition of zero in a localization allows. Their product $a=\prod_ja_j$ is nonzero and kills $Q$; for $Q=0$ use $a=1$. Regard $a$ as a nonzero element of $S$. It is fixed once and for all, before choosing a modification.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; claim: clearing the finitely many denominators explicitly, including the zero-cokernel case.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary normal modification $u:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. By [lem-per-normal-cover-point-blowup-refinement] choose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a sequence of point blowups and $q:Z\to X$ finite, with $Z$ the normalization in $L$ and $h:Z\to Y$ proper birational over $S$. Let $v=uh:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. This is a normal modification. All canonical modules and proper traces below are normalized relative to the same $W[2]$, using [lem-per-coherent-normal-surface-trace-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; last paragraph: passage to a finite covering model after point blowups.

proof.text: The sheaf $\Omega_{X/A_0}$ is coherent: on a chart that is a finite-type $R$-algebra generated by $z_1,\ldots,z_t$, its differential module is generated by the finitely many generators of $\Omega_{R/A_0}$ and $\mathrm dz_1,\ldots,\mathrm dz_t$; the chart is Noetherian, so kernels of maps from finite free modules to this finite module are finite, proving coherence. The same argument applies to $Z$, which is finite type over $R$, and to exterior powers, so finite adjunction below applies to the coherent source. Apply [lem-per-inseparable-differential-trace] to $q$ and then [lem-per-blowup-differentials-dualizing] to $X$ to obtain $q_*\Omega^r_{Z/A_0}\to(\Omega^r_{X/A_0})^{**}\xrightarrow{\varphi_X}\omega_X$. Finite adjunction from [lem-per-coherent-normal-surface-trace-calculus] gives $c_Z:\Omega^r_{Z/A_0}\to\omega_Z$. Its generic restriction is precisely the adjoint of the same differential trace as in Step 3: both models use $L/K$ and $\varphi_X$ is the identity at the generic point.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; last paragraph: constructing c_Y (here c_Z) from the reflexive differential trace and phi_X.

proof.text: For $\alpha\in\Omega^r_{S/A_0}$ pull the form back to $Z$ and apply $c_Z$, obtaining a section $\sigma_\alpha\in\Gamma(Z,\omega_Z)$. Its proper trace $\tau_v(\sigma_\alpha)$ equals $c(\alpha)$: at the generic point $v$ is the identity on $L$, its dualizing trace is the identity, and the two finite-adjoint maps have the same generic differential trace by Step 7. The target $\omega_S$ is torsion-free, so equality at that generic point implies equality in $\omega_S$, by [lem-per-coherent-normal-surface-trace-calculus]. Consequently $\operatorname{im}c\subseteq\operatorname{im}\tau_v$. The same node's trace-composition formula gives $\tau_v=\tau_u\circ\Gamma(\tau_h)$, hence $\operatorname{im}c\subseteq\operatorname{im}\tau_u$ for the original, arbitrary $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; last paragraph: explicit compatibility with the proper trace and descent from the dominating model.

proof.text: Since $\operatorname{im}c\subseteq\operatorname{im}\tau_u$, the cokernel of $\tau_u$ is a quotient of $Q$ and is killed by the fixed nonzero $a$ of Step 5. This holds for every normal modification $u$. Apply [lem-per-dualizing-trace-annihilator-bound] with $A=S$ and $W=\omega_S$. Step 2 supplies the normal local Nagata surface hypotheses and Step 3 supplies the normalized dualizing complex. It gives one integer bounding $\operatorname{length}_S H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ for all normal modifications. By [def-per-rational-surface-singularity] this is exactly reduction to rational singularities for $S$.

source.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p; final two sentences: fixed annihilator and application of Tag 0B4S.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B4U, resolve-lemma-go-up-degree-p, entire proof; explicit finite-generator annihilator and trace compatibility details supplied.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-a3f63768c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all six new nodes and every cited statement in full, against Stacks resolve.tex 0B4U (statement and whole proof), 0B4S, 0B4T, trace-well-defined/0AX5/0AX6, 0AXL and 0AHI. The item statement is 0B4U unchanged. Steps 1-9 follow the source. Step 1 is the first paragraph of 0B4U; I re-derived the differential-data node: with a p-basis t_i of k/k', A is free of rank p^{e+2} over A0, so Ω_{A/A0} is free on dt_i, dx, dy. Step 2: complete-local-excellence, then normal-surface-cover (first clause), regular-normal, prime-unique (normal base, finite, purely inseparable) and maximal contraction show S is local; with quasi-excellent-nagata, S meets every hypothesis of the definition. Step 3 takes the regular and finite clauses of the calculus node and the 0AX6 trace; the coherence argument is correct. Step 4: I checked φ_i(g^j)=δ_ij θ in the cases j<i, j=i and j>i (g^{p-1-i+j}=f g^{j-i-1}), including p=2. Step 5 is elementary: ω_S⊗K = Hom_K(L, W_K), and one annihilator a is fixed before any modification (a=1 if Q=0). Steps 6-8: the refinement node is true (a normal modification is an isomorphism over the punctured spectrum, then 0B49, 0AHI and finite normalization); v is a normal modification; φ_X and the trace are generically the identity, so torsion-freeness and τ_v=τ_u∘τ_h give im c ⊆ im τ_u. Step 9: the 0B4S node with A=S and W=ω_S; the trace over base S equals the counit at ω_S[2]=v^!W[2]. I checked all new nodes on small cases (e=0, p=2, length-zero towers) and found them true. They are statement-only and not duplicates: the lem-trf finite-after-blowup and coherent-duality nodes and the lem-weil-pbc power-series nodes are weaker or partial inputs. Batch 5: the reach of lem-per-complete-local-excellence to lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary is pure commutative algebra (regular rings are universally catenary), not trace-formula or Poincaré-duality content. The parent already cites that node, and it was reviewed PASS (NH 8844778b), so I accept it.
